description: fixtures2/00420_enum_take_drop_split.fz drives ~5300 jobs in ~1.3s, schedule-dependent (jobs_ran 5598-5702), ends Fatal LowerNativeProgram. Isolated via --log-telemetry post-processing (drive elapsed_ns + per-job-kind/changed-fact histograms). VERIFIED: zero return-widening, max 4 ascents (healthy per-activation type ascent) — NOT the f98 graduate-to-any. Root is breadth: a several-hundred-activation closure (take/drop/split x List+Range x lambdas x recursive reduce bridge), where SealSemanticClosure re-walks the WHOLE closure on every settled-fact change (~342x) = O(closure x changes) monolithic reseal (downstream-monolith), amplified by spurious replacing-fact re-appearance churn from partial publication (~4040 None->Some re-publishes). RED gate test: compiler2_enum_take_drop_split_seals_without_reseal_runaway (seal<=32, total<1500, Resolved). Sound cumulative fix lands but doesn't close it; replacing-fact preserve is unsound (claims overwritten value, unknown-is-not-none). Closure needs the foundational levers in child tickets.

comments.text: SPIKE SYNTHESIS (3 worktree spikes complete). The runaway is structural, not a bug in one fact: (1) fz-f98.14.3 CLOSED - the 281-activation closure is the LEGITIMATE size of this program (linear ~14+9.2*calls; all key dims dispatch-relevant); over-specialization ruled out by hard numbers, so collapsing activations is NOT the path. (2) The cost is O(closure^2): a monolithic seal re-walks the whole 281-activation closure ~346x. CLOSING THE RED GATE NEEDS BOTH ENGINE CHANGES, complementary: fz-f98.14.1 (incremental/cone-scoped seal via ActivationClosed fact + fan-in barrier, mirror transport fz-bfh.5) gets seal<=32; fz-f98.14.2 (two-tier provisional/committed publication decoupled from waits, kills the replacing-fact retraction->rebase cascade) gets total<1500 + Resolved/clears the Fatal. Both grounded in existing precedents (transport split; extend_outputs/mark_dirty). Sequence 14.1 first or together. The RED gate compiler2_enum_take_drop_split_seals_without_reseal_runaway re-enables only when both land.

COORDINATOR SIGNAL 2026-07-10: current enum_take_drop_split no longer matches only the old monolithic-reseal/LoweNativeProgram fatal. The fixture remains red because the interp leg is blocked by fz-k22.9 (ambiguous runtime closure identity) and the native leg is blocked by fz-f98.14.11 (incompatible callable materialization ABI on the same fixture). Added both as explicit blockers so this parent does not appear ready until the remaining fixture blockers close.

BOOKKEEPING CORRECTION 2026-07-10: bw rejected fz-f98.14.11 -> fz-f98.14 because descendants cannot block ancestors. The explicit blockers are now fz-k22.9 for enum_take_drop_split::interp ambiguity and fz-f98.6 for the native boxed-callable multi-surface/ABI incoherence. fz-f98.14.11 retains the concrete native return-lane evidence as a child note, but the non-descendant dependency edge is fz-f98.6.

MATRIX REDS CLEARED at d828560c9 (fz-qe0, PR #91) -- NOT CLOSING; the convergence root this ticket owns is still open.

WHAT CHANGED. All three enum_take_drop_split lanes are GREEN:
  test matrix::enum_take_drop_split::run    ... ok
  test matrix::enum_take_drop_split::interp ... ok
  test matrix::enum_take_drop_split::build  ... ok
Full matrix 410 passed / 0 failed single-threaded.

They were failing on WALL CLOCK, and fz-qe0 removed a cost shared by every Enum-heavy fixture: the recursive-group gate ran a full DFS over the entire product dependency graph per dependency per production (21.9M node visits) where it only ever needed the unsettled products, since a settled product answers a read immediately and no chain of waits runs through it. 21.9M -> 9.9K node visits, same cycles found.

So the lanes were red for a reason OUTSIDE this ticket's diagnosis, and that reason is gone.

WHAT DID NOT CHANGE. The fixture still takes 4.4s interp / 5.3s run / 5.4s build. By the standing convention that is still a correctness signal, and it is this ticket's O(closure x changes) monolithic reseal plus partial-publication churn -- untouched. fz-f98.14.2 (deadlock-safe settled-gating of replacing-fact publication) is still the open lever, and the blockers fz-f98.5 / fz-f98.9 / fz-f98.10 still stand.

STALE REFERENCES, re-verify before acting on this ticket:
- The RED gate named in the body, compiler2_enum_take_drop_split_seals_without_reseal_runaway, NO LONGER EXISTS anywhere in src/. There is nothing to 're-enable when both land'. A new gate has to be written, and it should assert against telemetry (job/settle census) rather than wall clock, since wall clock is what just moved for an unrelated reason.
- The 2026-07-10 coordinator signal says the fixture is red because interp is blocked by fz-k22.9 and native by fz-f98.14.11/fz-f98.6. All three lanes now pass, so those explanations no longer describe the observed state either -- re-derive before treating them as live.

The current excess-work population on the neighbouring Enum fixture is measured in fz-xat (2625 callable_construction settlements for 242 executables); the same census on this fixture is probably the cheapest next signal for this ticket.
